verifier.evidence: All six Febrex Plus presentations (tablet, syrup, AF syrup, DS suspension, drops, AF drops) are listed on this pharmacy. Our record names no dosage form, so no single product page can be selected without guessing.
verifier.notes: DOSAGE-FORM AMBIGUITY. Our catalogue name is plain 'Febrex Plus' with no form, and our own description reads 'Paracetamol-based syrup AND tablet combination', naming both forms. Febrex Plus ships as tablet (paracetamol 500 + phenylephrine 10 + chlorpheniramine 2), plain syrup, AF syrup, DS suspension, drops and AF drops, which differ in composition and in strength. This is the same situation as medicine 22 (Digene), which is already deprioritised for exactly this reason. Recommended for DEPRIORITIZED_IDS. Our composition field lists only 'Acetaminophen', a known artifact of the RxNorm ingredient reduction, so it cannot break the tie either.

verifier.evidence: Live page is titled 'Panderm ++ Cream', not 'Panderm Plus Cream'; Macleods Pharmaceuticals Ltd.
verifier.notes: AMBIGUOUS PRODUCT IDENTITY -- catalogue-quality issue flagged for separate investigation, NOT corrected. Our name is 'Panderm Plus Cream', which does not distinguish 'Panderm +' from 'Panderm ++', and our record has no composition. Apollo, 1mg and Netmeds all serve the '++' product (clobetasol 0.05% + miconazole 2% + neomycin 0.5%) under a panderm-plus slug, while a separate 'Panderm +' product also exists. Decisively, PharmEasy serves TWO different products that both render the display title 'Panderm Plus Cream', both from Macleods, with verified-different compositions: /panderm-plus-plus-cream-15gm-212766 is clobetasol + miconazole + neomycin, and /panderm-plus-cream-15gm-17432 is clobetasol + ofloxacin + ornidazole + terbinafine (PharmEasy salt group 321). Three-pharmacy agreement was NOT treated as sufficient: the name our catalogue holds maps to a four-drug product on one pharmacy and a three-drug product on the others. Our description ('steroid-based cream for eczema and other inflammatory skin conditions') fits both. Panderm NM, Panderm Super, Panderm V Gel and the Panderm dusting powders were also rejected.

verifier.evidence: Apollo's plain 'Polybion Syrup' page (HTTP 200) names the manufacturer as 'Merck Ltd', which does not match catalogue 'Procter & Gamble Health'.
verifier.notes: No plain 'Polybion Syrup' product is offered at 1mg, Netmeds or PharmEasy -- the brand there is sold only as Polybion LC (adds lysine), Polybion Active (sugar-free B-complex + lysine), Polybion SF / SF Complete (sugar-free) and Osto Polybion (adds calcium and vitamin D), each a different composition. Apollo does still list a plain 'Polybion Syrup', but its manufacturer field reads 'Merck Ltd', the pre-acquisition name: Merck's Indian consumer-health business became Procter & Gamble Health Ltd, which is the value our catalogue holds and which 1mg confirms on the Polybion SF page (procter-gamble-health-ltd). This is a stale marketer field on Apollo, not a catalogue error, and it was rejected rather than accepted -- the same treatment given to the Apollo and PharmEasy Practin pages that still name Wockhardt. Our catalogue value is correct and is NOT being changed.
